name: Cidade Velha
tagline: The old city, the market and the cathedral
description: The historic quarter where Belem began, holding the Forte do Presepio, the cathedral, the Casa das Onze Janelas and, at its edge, the Ver-o-Peso market. It is the most atmospheric part of the city and its restoration has moved in fits and starts.
bestFor: Anyone here for the old city and the market
pros: Ver-o-Peso and the colonial core on foot
River views and the Estacao das Docas nearby
The cheapest eating in the city
cons: Restoration is uneven, some blocks are derelict

name: Nazare
tagline: The mango-lined avenues and the basilica
description: The most desirable residential district, along the wide tree-lined avenues that give Belem its nickname as the city of mango trees, centred on the Basilica of Nossa Senhora de Nazare where the Cirio procession ends each October.
bestFor: Anyone prioritising safety and comfort over price
pros: The safest and most attractive district
Deep shade from the mango avenues
Good restaurants and the basilica nearby
cons: The most expensive rents in Belem

name: Umarizal
tagline: The high-rise district with the newest buildings
description: The modern residential district north of the centre, dense with apartment towers, the city's best supermarkets and a run of restaurants and bars aimed at the professional population. It has the most reliable infrastructure in Belem.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting reliable services and a modern flat
pros: Good security in the residential towers

name: Batista Campos
tagline: The park district between the old and new city
description: A residential neighbourhood built around the Praca Batista Campos, one of the city's best parks with its lakes and enormous trees. It sits between the old city and the modern towers and offers a compromise on price and safety between the two.
bestFor: Anyone wanting a park and a central position at a fair price
pros: One of the city's finest parks at the door
Between the old city and the modern district

name: Icoaraci
tagline: The riverside district with the ceramics and the boats
description: A district on the bay about twenty kilometres north of the centre, historically a separate town, with a working riverfront, boats to Ilha do Marajo and a Marajoara ceramics tradition still practised in workshops along its streets.
bestFor: Anyone drawn to the ceramics or heading to Marajo
pros: Boats to Ilha do Marajo leave from here
Much cheaper than the central districts
cons: Forty minutes from the centre in traffic
Safety requires the same caution as the centre
